newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-opera official on trial for manslaughter in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Ex-opera official on trial for manslaughter in Paris.

text.p: A state prosecutor on Friday asked a Paris criminal court to order suspended prison terms against managers of the Paris Bastille Opera over the fatal collapse of a set during a 1992 rehearsal in Seville, Spain.
A member of the opera chorus, Annick Taffary, was killed in the accident and 39 singers and technicians were hurt.

Prosecutor Alain Blanchot requested a three-month suspended sentence against Pierre Berge, then-director of the Bastille opera and now chairman of the Yves Saint Laurent fashion house, for failing to set up a safety committee at the opera.
But he left the court free to keep or drop the charge of manslaughter against Berge.

He asked for suspended sentences of 15 months against Technical Director Jean-Michel Dubois and two others, and of 12 months for former general manager Georges-Francois Hirsch, director Petrika Ionesco and two others.
The lawyer for Taffary's relatives accused the opera company of making petty savings on safety and rushing a production without regard for security.
"There was a terrifying atmosphere of contempt which reigned at the opera. It was not by chance that this accident occurred, it was unavoidable," said Marie-Madeleine Tusseau.
The set collapsed when the Bastille opera company was rehearsing for a performance of Verdi's "Otello" as part of Seville's Expo 92 universal exhibition cultural programme.
The trial ended on Friday. No date has been set for the verdict.
